applies_why: The judge text addresses a collision in which the challenger's own footed chain is pressed against the link, and it resolves that collision by saying the sentence's own words state the source.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: I weighed whether relying on the sentence's own words is proper chain-against-chain footing or is the prohibited verse-by-verse resolution.
why: The judge resolves the collision by the sentence's own wording rather than by weighing the challenger's footed chain against the defended chain by footing.
